newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $70-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $70-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Monday were seen priced at $69.00 to $70.00 per cwt following active sales this week at $68.00, feedlot sources said.

This week's hefty trade depleted showlists, with some owners pulling cattle from next week's lists to meet the strong packer demand, several cattle feeder said. As a result, next week's showlists were seen steady to smaller than this week, which could lend support to cattle prices.
Sales were reported Friday at $68.00 in limited activity, sources in some areas said.
About 3,000 head sold Friday in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area and about 500 in Kansas.

Prices next week also could be supported by outlooks for continued strength in beef prices, some sources noted. Beef demand was seen firm the next few weeks on a seasonal basis as retailers book orders for Memorial Day, May 26, holiday advertisements.

Beef prices Friday were quoted up $0.54 to $0.67 per cwt, on 258 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice was quoted up $0.55 at $106.23, up $1.61 for the week, USDA statistics showed.
There were 1,330 total fabricated beef loads reported by USDA sold this week versus 1,342 last week.
